decidability_statement.headline: NO — `sequence` is NOT decidable as a game quantity from the permitted evidence.
decidability_statement.why: `sequence` is engine bookkeeping: an event-ordering ordinal internal to the coupled participant timeline. It is not a League of Legends quantity. It appears nowhere in the cached wiki text under data/ (items.json, champions.json, runes.json, the atom and wiki caches carry stats, effect text, scalings and provenance — no event-ordering counter), and it appears nowhere in docs/math-foundations.md, which documents damage/mitigation/timeline MATH (§2 resistance composition, §3 BIS optimization, the §5 exactness table) and never specifies an event-record schema or how ordinals are assigned. Grepping math-foundations for 'sequence' returns only unrelated prose ('shared hit sequence', a cited paper title). No computation over cached wiki data can yield the integer 34, nor the integer 7, nor any other.
decidability_statement.what_IS_decidable: Identity is decidable, and identity is enough to settle which of the two offered values can be a value OF THIS EVENT. See the structural analysis below. Correctness of the ordinal-assignment scheme itself remains outside this evidence tree and is flagged as such.

step_1_read_the_committed_ordinals.pattern: Two disjoint ordinal bands are visible in the committed data. LOW band {1, 5, 7} attaches to base ability casts (Lulu Q, Jax W, Jax E). HIGH band {30, 33, 34, 35} attaches to derived rows — the W on-hit and the Bloodsong proc chain. The value 7 sits in the low, cast-allocated band and is already occupied, within this same attacker's stream (`main`) against this same target, by the Jax E cast at t=9.5.

step_2_the_proc_chain_is_internally_cont.chain: At the single instant t=7.5 the Bloodsong causal chain runs spellblade (33) -> expose_weakness physical (34) -> expose_weakness magic (35), immediately after the W cast (5) that armed the spellblade.
step_2_the_proc_chain_is_internally_cont.wiki_grounding: This ordering is what the item text requires: the debuff is inflicted BY the empowered attack ('If the target is a champion, inflict them with Expose Weakness'; the 1.5s cooldown 'starts after using the empowered attack'). So the spellblade row must precede the amplification rows it causes, and the two typed amplification rows are siblings of one application. 33 -> 34 -> 35 realises that causal order with no gap.
step_2_the_proc_chain_is_internally_cont.consequence: Substituting 7 for the subject's ordinal would (a) pull an item-proc row into the cast band, (b) duplicate the E cast's ordinal within the same attacker/target stream, and (c) break the contiguous 33/34/35 chain by leaving 33 and 35 straddling an ordinal from a different band and a later timestamp (9.5). 34 is the only offered value consistent with the committed neighbourhood.

step_3_where_the_new_value_actually_come.observation: The pre-change record at index [84] is main:enemy:Aatrox:35 — attacker main, t=9.5, sequence 7, source "E", damage_type magic, skipped_reason "outside_window".
step_3_where_the_new_value_actually_come.arithmetic: S6/S7 removed two events from this 85-record list at positions at or before 82. Removing two members shifts old[84] into new[82]. old[84].sequence = 7 and old[84].damage_type = 'magic' are EXACTLY the two 'new values' the brief offers across this cluster's two leaves.
step_3_where_the_new_value_actually_come.inference: Both leaves of this cluster are a single reading of one ordinal substitution, not two independent numeric changes. 'sequence 34 -> 7' compares the Bloodsong Expose Weakness amplification row against the Jax E cast. The two ordinals are unrelated; there is no quantity of which 34 and 7 are competing estimates.
step_3_where_the_new_value_actually_come.removal_hypothesis: The cleanest explanation of a two-event removal that puts old[84] at new[82] is that the removed pair is exactly [82] and [83] — the two expose_weakness_Bloodsong rows. If so, the subject event is a REMOVED member, and a removal is a membership transition, not a value change: its `sequence` did not become 7, it ceased to be present. That is reported as its own transition, per the cluster's stated remedy, and it does not make 7 a value of this event. This receipt does not adjudicate whether the removal itself is correct — that question is about engine attribution policy and lies outside the permitted evidence tree.

verdict_reasoning: Constrained to {new_value_correct | old_value_correct | both_wrong} and adjudicating against the event identified as main:enemy:Aatrox:33, only 'old_value_correct' is defensible. `sequence` is not a game quantity and cannot be derived from cached wiki text or docs/math-foundations.md, so no computation certifies 34 as the uniquely right ordinal — that undecidability is stated explicitly above and is the answer to the question the brief asked. What the permitted evidence plus the committed identity DO settle is that 7 is not this event's sequence: 7 is the ordinal of the Jax E cast at t=9.5 (old index [84]), it sits in the cast-allocated low band while this row sits in the derived/proc high band, and adopting it would duplicate an ordinal already held in the same attacker stream and break the causally required contiguous 33/34/35 chain that the Bloodsong item text mandates. 'both_wrong' is unavailable because no evidence contradicts 34 — it is the ordinal this event carries and it is consistent with every visible neighbour. So: 34 stands as this event's sequence; 7 is an artifact of ordinal re-indexing and is a reading of a different record.
confidence_qualification: Verdict scope is deliberately narrow. It certifies that the offered new value belongs to a different event and that the old value is consistent with the committed neighbourhood. It does NOT certify the engine's ordinal-allocation scheme as correct, because no permitted source describes that scheme. Any downstream reviewer who wants the scheme itself audited must pose that as a question about src/, not as a golden-baseline leaf.

supersedes_prior_brief_defect.defect: R-18 addressed this leaf purely by ordinal (/combat/events[82]/sequence) with two bare values and no event identity — no event_id, no timestamp, no source, no list length — while forbidding the tree that would expose the substitution. Because S6/S7 removed two earlier events from cleaver_bloodsong_roster, leaf_report paired the OLD snapshot's events[82] with the NEW snapshot's events[82] although they are different events, so 'sequence 34 -> 7' compared two unrelated ordinals. The posed question had no single referent. Both prior investigators detected this and wrote the caveat into their own receipts, which is why it is recorded as a brief defect rather than a wrong verdict; it is the first realization of the hazard the P4-boundary entry later hit in its second form.
supersedes_prior_brief_defect.remedy_applied_here: This re-adjudication addresses the record by event_id main:enemy:Aatrox:33 and supplies the R-15/R-18 amendment's timestamp/ordinal/trigger-context clause: t=7.5, sequence 34, source expose_weakness_Bloodsong, with neighbours [81] spellblade seq 33 and [83] expose_weakness seq 35. That trigger context is what makes the ordinal band structure visible and what lets an oracle demonstrate — rather than merely suspect — that 7 belongs to the E cast at old index [84].
